text_blocks.snippet: While the World Health Organization (WHO) declared an end to the COVID-19 public health emergency of international concern (PHEIC) on May 5, 2023, whether it is still considered a pandemic is a matter of ongoing debate among experts. COVID-19 continues to circulate, and the definition of a pandemic and its end points are not universally agreed upon.

list.title: WHO's Declaration:
list.snippet: The WHO's declaration ending the PHEIC signifies a shift in how the global community manages COVID-19, moving away from a state of emergency towards a more sustained approach.

list.title: Ongoing Circulation:
list.snippet: COVID-19 is still present and continues to cause illness and deaths, meaning it hasn't disappeared entirely.

list.title: Defining a Pandemic:
list.snippet: There isn't a single, universally accepted definition of when a pandemic begins or ends. Some experts may focus on disease prevalence and impact, while others may focus on the public health response.

list.title: Debate Among Experts:
list.snippet: The question of whether COVID-19 is still a pandemic depends on the specific definition used and the criteria being applied.
